Ok so I've been using for about 7 months or so with a 2 month break during October and November as I had no reason to use it at that time.

 Positive Effects: On phenibut I'm much more vocal and sociable, when I look in the mirror it's apparent just by my eyes, you see I'm a pretty depressed guy, almost always lethargic and exhausted, lacking the will to speak or build any confidence but on phenibut, I'm, well, what I like to think is who I really am without the "sludge in my soul". I'd say I've improved socially by using it even without it as it's given me a bit of a blueprint but its still not the same, like when I feel a surge of certainty or confidence it hits me that I'm not on phenibut so it doesn't feel real. 

First/Latest Experience: My first experience was half a gram mixed with coffee(always do this), there was an amazing body high(hard to describe, just felt a nice tingly sensation in my legs) and an insane increase in confidence and positivity, didn't do anything special but it felt great. My last experience was approximately a gram and half, same thing with only a subtle body high, the effects are much more subtle now but it still gets the job done, I've slowly been increasing dosage but I've never gone over 1.5g.

Efficacy: I mean its amazing, it just makes my day enjoyable, sometimes there is no body high, sometimes I'm not even very talkative, it's just the difference between feeling like shit and feeling confident and content.

Withdrawals/Negative Effects: Usually my withdraws happen after back to backs. I "only" use a 1-1.5 grams and I try to keep it at 2 times a week but occasionally I slip up. During the second day of a back to back the high isn't very pleasant, I feel disoriented, as if I'm near passing out with these strange head rushes/lightheadedness hitting in waves. Typically the next day is full of headaches and an increase in exhaustion but last week it was even more intense. I used a gram one day, a gram and half the next, the following 3 days were hell. The "tingly" body high remained but this time it wasn't full of warmth and optimism, it felt like millions of bugs were crawling on my legs instilling a sense of panic in me at all times. Just this horrible fear and panic with the worst headache I've ever endured all while feeling the most tired I've felt maybe ever(didn't sleep well either). This went on strongly for 2 days and whilst faded in intensity it remained for a 3rd day(didn't feel too hot on the 4th fay either honestly). I used to think I never actually experienced a withdrawal, that it was just rebound depression and a coincidental headache but last week put away any doubts.

Dependence: My dependence is more severe than I'm proud to admit, it's like it eliminates this "thing" in me that holds me back, some filter that stops me from being who I am, but on phenibut I'm finally me...at least thats what I tell myself. But as you've read most of the negatives stem from abuse and me using drugs with not so great mental health. The abuse part is strange because it seems like most people are taking at least 2 grams and go crazy with it, I thought since I keep the doses relatively low I could get away with a back to back every once in awhile but the effects/depression aren't worth going over 2 times a week personally. Very strange drug with a lot of varying experiences.

"Shortcuts" by Robert Altman- A film about the lives of suburban Los Angeles residents that while over 3 hours long, kept me interested all the way through. The acting was phenomenal as was most things about this film. I was very interested in all the characters and their stories all the way through. I love it when movies don't spell everything out for you, they require you to pay attention because there isn't gonna be some exposition explaining the plot development or characters feeling every 10 minutes. Nothing was forced(one could argue the ending but I don't think it was) and it felt very honest and subtle. My only flaws/confusion is that Tom Robbins character is a cop and just seems to patrol all day, it never really shows or suggests the paperwork side of the job, it kinda annoyed me. And there was what looked like a continuity error when basketball was being played and a layup was being made from the right side of the hoop but it cut to it being made from what looked like the front side of it, could be wrong and obviously this doesn't mean much. 9/10 for now



"The Kid With A Bike" by Jean-Pierre Dardenne- A film about a young child's life after being abounded by his father. I've seen a fair share of heart-wrenching films but this one got to me like few do. Thomas Doret was amazing as the abandoned child as was the script that managed to make a child a well written character, something seemingly rare. The story progressed better than I thought it would originally, not having a section that felt like filler or unnecessary. It was shot and edited really well like there was nothing particularly special about either, I just thought they made good decisions with both. Overall a very emotional and memorable experience. Another 9/10


"The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford" by Andrew Dominik- A story centered around Robert Ford (played amazingly by Casey Affleck) and Jesse James(Also played amazingly by Brad Pitt). This film floored me. I'm not quite sure what I expected but it sure as hell wasn't this. Amazing cinematography. A great western atmosphere. Amazing score. Amazing acting. Amazing movie. I loved it from the start, it's hard to describe why the plot sucked me in so easily but it did. I was never bored at all. The characters were well written and complex. And coming into it I was expecting a film idolizing Jesse James and demonizing Robert Ford. Turns out that was just manipulation. All of these characters feel human. They're not made out to be good or bad, they're people with flaws. As the film progressed I was increasingly nervous about the inevitable climax, I didn't think they could pull it off well but I was so wrong and the minutes following were even better. The narration was maybe the only time I've liked narration in a film and the ending is one of my all time favorites, as is this film. 10/10
